**Notes from The Critic:**
- Seven weeks, 29 dish ratings; 24 of 29 at 4★+. Four "Cook again: No" verdicts (Cuban pork chops, Lomo Saltado, Greek meatball bowls) plus the first-ever 1★ (Creamy Cajun Shrimp Pasta).
- **REHEAT QUALITY IS A FIRST-CLASS CRITERION — the biggest new signal.** Sean stated it plainly twice this week: these are two-portion meals, he is a single adult, and next-day-lunch leftovers are "almost my entire diet." Two of this week's stars were lost purely on reheat behavior — scallops "do not reheat well at all" (4★ instead of 5★) and butter chicken's yogurt "separates on reheat." **Recommendation to the Chef: treat next-day reheat as a scoring dimension when selecting dishes.** Favor braises, skillets, saucy grain/bean dishes, stews, roasts, ground-meat dishes. Use delicate quick-sear proteins (scallops, shrimp, thin fish) sparingly and preferably on a weekend when both portions get eaten fresh — and say so on the recipe card.
- **Yogurt cap escalates from advisory to hard rule for cream-sauce applications.** The 07-24 cap (~1 yogurt-forward sauce/week) was the right call; this week shows why. Greek yogurt as a *creamy pasta sauce base* produced the kitchen's only 1★ and the only uneaten meal — it broke against Cajun spice and it separates on reheat. New guidance: yogurt is fine as a *finishing* element or marinade (butter chicken, shawarma) at ~1/week; **never as the primary body of a creamy pasta or a spice-forward sauce.** Use heavy cream, coconut milk, tomato, or a pan-butter emulsion there.
- **Difficulty estimates broke their perfect streak.** After 23 straight dishes at "as expected" or "easier," week 07-20 produced the first **"harder than described"** — Chimichurri Flank Steak, on the specific step of cooking a whole flank steak to medium-rare. Also: Ginger-Sesame Turkey Lettuce Wraps were billed as quick but took ~40 minutes. **Recommendation: when a recipe calls for a whole steak, include an explicit doneness method (high heat, thermometer target ~130–135°F, rest time). And stop labeling multi-component wrap/bowl assemblies as ≤30-minute weeknight meals — Sean's real-world times run long on those.**
- **Shopping-list → Instacart quantity translation is now a three-time recurring failure.** Week 06-08 omitted honey, sesame seeds, and rice wine vinegar; week 07-20 under-delivered lemons (list called for several, one arrived) and cherry tomatoes (Sean had to make a store run). The list content appears correct — the loss is happening in the Instacart hand-off, likely on multi-unit produce. **Recommendation: state produce counts explicitly and prominently (e.g. "LEMONS ×3 — you need all three") and flag any item where a shortfall would break the dish.**
- **Sauce-sopper insight worth reusing:** Sean invented a serving trick for the Italian sausage skillet — warmed baguette slices stood around the rim of the bowl to soak up sauce. He called it a "perfect use case." Adopt it on the recipe card, and consider crusty bread as a deliberate component of future saucy skillet/stew dishes.
- **User mod to carry forward:** for Ginger-Sesame Turkey Lettuce Wraps, Sean wants to try spinach tortilla wraps instead of lettuce, and the sauce needs thickening (cornstarch slurry or a reduction step) — it ran runny and messy.
- Protein-format signal, not protein signal — now confirmed four ways: pork chops missed (3★/No) while ground pork scored 4★; Lomo Saltado missed while every other beef format is 5★ (chimichurri steak 5★ this week); Greek meatballs missed on the yogurt/tzatziki format while chicken is otherwise 5★; and Cajun shrimp missed on a yogurt cream sauce, not on shrimp. **Judge formats and sauces, not proteins.**
- Mississippi Pot Roast is 5★ twice — a locked-in permanent favorite; the "4 meals of leftovers" value is exactly the reheat-friendly profile Sean needs. Last served 07-13, so it comes back into range around week 08-10.
- Garlic-butter chicken + broccoli remains 2-for-2 at 5★; adopt Sean's mods (pasta added, broccoli par-boiled) into the recipe card next time it's served.
- Never-cooked early-reuse pool: **Cajun Honey-Butter Shrimp Bowls (dropped 06-29)** — still technically eligible, but now carries risk by association: it is Cajun and shrimp, the two nouns attached to the 1★. It is honey-butter, not yogurt-cream, so the actual failure mode does not apply — but it should not be the Chef's first pick, and if used it must be well separated from any other Cajun or shrimp dish.
- Carry-forward operational reminder: no new list-gap categories beyond produce quantities.

## Recipe Recycling Rules
*The Chef reads these when building the weekly menu.*

- ★★★★★ (5): Recycle every 3–4 weeks
- ★★★★ (4): Recycle every 5–6 weeks
- ★★★ (3): Recycle only if explicitly carried over
- ★★ (2) or below: Do not recycle unless Sean requests it
- "Cook again: No" overrides star rating — do not recycle regardless of score
